title: Health & pharmacy
body:
Emergency numbers: Police 110, Fire/Ambulance 119 — both work nationwide, English support is limited but dispatchers can usually connect a translator. Save these before you land.

Pharmacies (Matsumoto Kiyoshi, Sugi, Tsuruha) are everywhere in Tenjin, Susukino, and around Sendai Station, but English-speaking pharmacists are the exception outside Tokyo — bring any prescriptions in their original labeled packaging, and a doctor's note if you carry anything that could read as a controlled substance (some common US allergy/ADHD medications are restricted in Japan).

Hokkaido and Tohoku in late Oct/Nov run cold — Sapporo's average first snow lands late October, and mountain trail areas (Jozankei's harder routes, Zao) can see snow before that. Pack real layers and waterproof footwear for the hiking days.

Earthquakes: Japan is seismically active nationwide, and Tohoku specifically was the epicenter region of the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake — the 2 continuing to Sendai will visit stops (Naruko Gorge's shortened trail, coastal Matsushima) that still carry visible aftereffects. If a quake hits: drop, cover, hold on; away from the coast there's no tsunami risk, but Matsushima is a coastal stop — know the nearest high ground if you're there when one happens.

US State Dept travel advisory: could not be confirmed — the page is bot-gated against automated fetches and needs a live browser check. Check travel.state.gov directly before you go — it's on the booking checklist above.
